A CRITICAL crack reading here should be read as 'refined-product price stress confirmed', not 'refinery/logistics root cause confirmed' — that requires the inventory/utilization series this deployment doesn't yet pull independently of market_mechanics.py.
falsification_conditions: If diesel cracks normalize while inventories stabilize and refinery utilization recover, downgrade the product-scarcity thesis even if crude remains elevated. (Inventory/utilization confirmation is not wired into this module — see data_quality_notes.)

A crack spread computed from mismatched units, mismatched delivery months/dates, or a futures-vs-physical mismatch is a DATA_QUALITY_FAILURE, not a signal, by construction of matched_crack_spread() in godseye_modules_common.py.

panels.title: Country Vulnerability Matrix
panels.trend_1w: insufficient history — module_results table needs >=2 dated rows; see schema_v3_extension_modules.sql
countervailing_evidence: All 19 country profiles are unpopulated seeds (every field=None). This module's scoring engine is fully functional and tested (see tests/test_godseye_modules.py), but produces DATA_QUALITY_FAILURE for every country until a maintainer loads real values from FAO/USDA FAS/World Bank WDI/WFP/IMF — see MODULES_README.md. This is intentional: the alternative was hardcoding the vault's own prior qualitative risk list (Bangladesh, Pakistan, Somalia, Sudan, Afghanistan, Yemen, etc.) as if it were sourced numeric data, which the spec explicitly prohibits.
falsification_conditions: A country's overall_score can only rise if its own sourced fields indicate rising vulnerability — this module cannot be moved by narrative alone.
If field_coverage is low for a country, its overall_state should be read as 'insufficient data', not 'low risk' — see field_coverage in each country's result.
